topics.title: Temperature & Humidity Effects on Distance
topics.subtitle: How air density changes your carry and total yardage
topics.defaultPrompt: Help me understand how temperature and humidity affect my golf ball distance. TrackMan data shows that air density — driven by temperature, humidity, and altitude — directly changes carry distance. Cold dry air is denser and reduces carry, while hot humid air is thinner and increases it. I want to understand the actual yardage differences so I can club properly. How many yards do I gain or lose per 10-degree temperature change? Does humidity really make the ball go farther, and by how much? How do temperature and humidity combine with altitude?
topics.promptTemplate: Explain how temperature and humidity affect golf ball carry distance and total distance. TrackMan measures air density from temperature, humidity, and barometric pressure, and uses it to calculate ball flight. Cold dense air creates more drag and reduces carry; hot humid air is less dense and increases carry. {{skill_level_context}} {{condition_context}} {{detail_level_context}}

options.label: Beginner
options.promptFragment: Keep the physics simple — just tell me the practical yardage adjustments for different conditions.

options.label: Intermediate
options.promptFragment: I understand that conditions affect distance. Give me the numbers — yards gained or lost per temperature and humidity change — so I can adjust my club selection.

options.label: Advanced
options.promptFragment: Include the aerodynamics — how air density affects drag coefficient and Magnus force on a spinning golf ball. Reference TrackMan's normalized vs. raw distance data and explain when normalization matters for practice vs. on-course decisions.

options.label: Temperature + Humidity Combined
options.promptFragment: Explain how temperature and humidity work together. For example, compare a 95°F day at 80% humidity versus a 45°F day at 20% humidity — what's the total distance difference for a 7-iron and a driver?

options.label: Temperature Only
options.promptFragment: Focus on temperature alone. How many yards of carry does a typical golfer gain or lose per 10°F (or 5°C) change? Give specific examples: a 7-iron that carries 160 yards at 70°F — what does it carry at 50°F and 90°F?

options.label: Humidity Only
options.promptFragment: Focus on humidity. Most golfers think humid air is heavier, but water vapor is actually lighter than dry air. Explain this counterintuitive physics and quantify the real distance effect — is it 1-2 yards or more significant?

options.label: Altitude + Temperature + Humidity
options.promptFragment: Cover the full picture: altitude, temperature, and humidity together. How do they compound? Compare sea level at 70°F to Denver (5,280 ft) at 90°F with high humidity — total yardage swing for a driver and a 7-iron.

options.label: Quick Reference Chart
options.promptFragment: Give me a simple reference chart: temperature ranges, humidity levels, and the approximate yards to add or subtract for a driver and a 7-iron.

options.label: Detailed Explanation
options.promptFragment: Explain the science behind air density effects on ball flight, with specific TrackMan-style numbers for carry distance changes across a range of conditions.

options.label: On-Course Strategy
options.promptFragment: Focus on practical on-course decision making: how to check conditions, estimate the combined effect, and adjust club selection. Include rules of thumb I can use without a calculator.
